To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
confirmatory factor analyses on longitudinal data can be done with a partial likelihood method, and that this method has a good asymptotic behavior for a broad class.

(1) the full likelihood method for confirmatory factor analysis on panel data is not feasible for the non–normal case; (2) the partial likelihood method is feasible, and has good statistical properties; and (3) the proposed method is superior to standard approaches.

confirmatory factor analysis of non–normal panel–data can be performed using partial likelihood, and that this method is superior to standard methods in terms of goodness of fit, robustness to non–normality and time trend, and computational efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to analyze panel data in a confirmatory factor analysis framework.
the application of confirmatory factor analyses to longitudinal non–normal data.
the problem of factor analysis of non–normal longitudinal data, and proposes a method based on a partially–specified model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the full likelihood method should be used for normal data, the partial likelihood method for non–normal panel or longitudinal data and the time– series modelling should be avoided for panel or longitudinal data.
the partial likelihood method is the best choice for factor analysis on longitudinal data, especially for the non–normal data.
the proposed partial likelihood method is superior to the standard methods for unbalanced panel data, and that the standard methods should be used only when the proposed method is not applicable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method proposed in this paper has several advantages over the standard methods for the analysis of longitudinal data.
the proposed method is very useful in analysing longitudinal data, especially when the number of measured subjects is not large and/or the number of measured occasions is not large.
the partial likelihood method has several advantages over other methods for the confirmatory factor analysis on non–normal multivariate longitudinal data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed methodology is a viable alternative to standard methods for the analysis of non–normal panel–data.
the proposed method is able to handle non–normal data and is able to provide a good fit to the data.
the partial likelihood method is more efficient than the standard time series methods.
